verdict: CBRE grew revenue 13% to $11.5B, led by building operations and surging data-center work, and a $184M gain on selling real estate helped lift GAAP profit 22% to $443M.

segments.name: Building Operations & Experience
segments.note: Running buildings for clients — facilities and property management. Reported segment revenue was $6,856M; the $18M of corporate eliminations is netted here so the lines tie. Critical infrastructure services revenue surged 80%, driven by data-center work and the Pearce Services acquisition.

segments.name: Advisory Services
segments.note: Leasing, property sales, mortgage origination, loan servicing and valuations. Global property sales revenue rose 28% and leasing 6%.

segments.name: Project Management
segments.note: Managing construction and fit-out projects for clients — growth tempered by slower corporate spending on real estate, while infrastructure program work stayed strong.

segments.name: Real Estate Investments
segments.note: Developing property (Trammell Crow) and managing investments for clients, with more than $155B of assets under management. Revenue dipped, but segment profit more than doubled on data-center land sales.

opex.name: Operating, administrative & other
opex.note: Staff and running costs not billed straight through to clients — includes $76M of acquisition integration costs and $35M of business and finance transformation costs.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Wear and tear on offices and systems, and amortization of intangibles from acquisitions.

otherDetail: A $184M gain on selling real estate, plus $104M of equity income from businesses CBRE part-owns and $8M of other income, less $62M of net interest expense and $37M of profit attributable to noncontrolling interests — net +$197M shown in the chart.
oneTimers: A $184M gain on disposition of real estate (vs $36M a year ago) is included in GAAP operating income as reported; this page shows it in Other income. It came mainly from development asset sales, including data-center land.

CBRE's headline core EPS of $2.05 (non-GAAP) excludes, among other items, $76M of acquisition integration costs, $56M of non-cash amortization of acquisition intangibles and $35M of transformation costs; core net income was $599M versus GAAP net income of $443M.

takeaways.title: Data centers are the growth story
takeaways.text: Critical infrastructure services revenue surged 80%, on data-center services demand and the Pearce acquisition (Nov 2025). Building Operations overall grew 17% to $6.9B and is now 60% of CBRE's revenue.

takeaways.title: Asset sales flattered GAAP profit
takeaways.text: A $184M gain on selling real estate — five times last year's — helped GAAP net income rise 22% to $443M. Strip out CBRE's list of one-offs and core net income was $599M, up 25%.

takeaways.title: Much of the revenue is pass-through
takeaways.text: Of the $11.5B top line, $4,691M is pass-through costs — subcontracted work for clients that CBRE bills back at no markup. That is why the profit margin on total revenue looks thin: the real service revenue is much smaller than the headline.

footerNote: Reported operating income of $561M includes the $184M gain on disposition of real estate; this page shows that gain in Other income, so the operating-profit block reads $377M. Net income is the $443M attributable to CBRE Group (total net income $480M, less $37M attributable to noncontrolling interests).
